setup_seconds.note: DECLARED planning figures, not measured on this rig. plan.measured_pace() replaces them from the session's own log once three observations of a cost class exist.

quality_defaults.notes: blur/clip/border/mean are capture/quality.py's own defaults, unchanged. max_scale_range_ratio is EXP_0043's PASS band.

shots.framing: 350 mm field framed so that BOTH sides of the asymmetric feature pair are inside one frame with the garment's centre line at frame centre (e.g. both back pockets, both belt loop groups, both knee fades). If the pair cannot fit at 350 mm, shoot the two members as .I01 and .I02 at identical framing and say so in the manifest.
shots.purpose: Construction asymmetry recorded BEFORE the cut is what stops a post-wash L/R difference being read as differential shrinkage or an uneven cut. Capturing both members in one frame with one board makes the comparison immune to the scale and tilt differences that two separate frames would introduce.

quality.extra: GATE_A. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed asymmetry_count integer. has_asymmetry is also the reason no L/R shot anywhere in this catalogue is merged or marked optional.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).

shots.scale_placement: Board coplanar with the backdrop, top-left frame corner, >=125x100 mm strip in frame, identically placed if the pair is split across two frames.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on distressing instance NN as enumerated in the record's existing_damage_annotations; the whole feature plus >=40 mm of undamaged denim on every side, and the nearest seam or hardware landmark inside the frame so the feature is relocatable. If the feature is longer than 160 mm, shoot overlapping frames R1..Rn with >=30% overlap. Garment face is bound at instantiation from the annotation's location field.
shots.purpose: Pre-existing distressing is loose or broken weave that will fray in the wash independently of anything the shears do, so an unrecorded instance becomes a false positive in the post-wash fray measurement. One frame per instance is the only way each is separately attributable.

quality.extra: GATE_B. INSTANCE SCHEME: .I01, .I02 ... zero-padded two digits, allocated at intake in the order the annotator enumerated existing_damage_annotations, and the same index written into the shot manifest so shot and annotation stay 1:1. Requires the proposed distressing_count integer -- conditional_on is a boolean expression and cannot say how many frames to demand.

shots.scale_placement: Steel rule on the denim beside the feature, coplanar, graduated edge facing it, within 20 mm, never crossing the damaged area.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on embroidery instance NN: the whole embroidered area, individual stitch penetrations resolvable at the densest point, the stabiliser/denim boundary, >=40 mm of plain denim around it, and the nearest seam landmark.
shots.purpose: Dense embroidery locally stiffens and pre-shrinks the ground fabric, so it is a shrinkage anomaly with a sharp boundary; its threads are also a different fibre that can bleed. Without a before frame at stitch resolution, post-wash puckering around it reads as fabric distortion.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on logo instance NN (woven tab, printed mark, stamped hardware logo): the whole logo with all text legible in the frame's own orientation, its attachment to the fabric, >=40 mm of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam landmark.
shots.purpose: Logos are the identity evidence that lets this exact garment be re-identified later, which is what the DATA_ELIGIBILITY exact_garment tri-state demands a written basis for; a verification nobody wrote down is not a verification. They are also small printed or woven elements that visibly degrade in a wash.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed logo_count integer. Legible brand text is also a provenance artefact -- it belongs in the garment's own record, not in any committed derived JSON, since committed artefacts carry numbers and manifests only.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on paint instance NN: the whole painted area if it fits, otherwise the most detailed 200 mm of it plus overlapping frames R1..Rn at >=30% overlap; every edge of the paint film, any existing cracking or flaking, >=40 mm of unpainted denim, and the nearest seam landmark.
shots.purpose: SEQUENCING CRITICAL: a painted print is what determines whether the garment can be machine-washed at all, and DENIM_0001 already took that branch. This frame must precede any wash decision, and it is the before-state of the component most likely to change visibly in the wash. Once washed, an uncracked before-state cannot be reconstructed.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed paint_count integer. DENIM_0001 has one painted seagull per back leg, i.e. paint_count = 2, and its record already carries the care guidance that put the whole garment on the hand-wash branch.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on applied-patch instance NN: the whole patch, its full attachment perimeter (stitched, fused or riveted), any lifting at the edges, >=40 mm of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam landmark.
shots.purpose: An applied patch is a second fabric with its own shrinkage rate bonded to the garment, and edge lifting is the most common wash failure; a fused patch can also release entirely. Its before-state perimeter is the only reference for judging that.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed patch_count integer. Distinct from WAIST.BRAND_PATCH, which is the waistband maker's patch and has its own dedicated shot.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on alteration instance NN (re-hem, taper, shortened leg, replaced hardware): the alteration stitch line, the ORIGINAL stitch holes or crease if still visible, >=40 mm of denim each side, and the nearest original seam for reference.
shots.purpose: A previous alteration means the garment's recorded dimensions are not its factory dimensions, and a previously re-hemmed leg has fabric that has already been through a hem's stress and possibly a wash. It invalidates the inseam-derived positions this whole catalogue uses, so it must be found and recorded before those positions are trusted.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed previous_alteration_count integer. If the alteration is a previous re-hem, original_inseam_cm in the record is NOT the garment's factory inseam and every position derived from it (knee at inseam/2, shin at 3/4 inseam) shifts -- the navigator must refuse to compute those positions silently and raise HUMAN_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED instead.

shots.scale_placement: Steel rule on the denim beside the alteration, coplanar, graduated edge facing it, within 20 mm.

shots.framing: 350 mm field centred on fade instance NN (whiskering fan, knee fade, honeycomb): the WHOLE fade pattern including its outer boundary where it returns to full-shade denim, plus the nearest seam so the pattern is relocatable. A 200 mm field is too small for a whisker fan, which is why this ANOM type uses the region tier.
shots.purpose: Fades are pre-existing shade gradients that a wash redistributes, so they are the strongest confound for any post-wash colour or shade measurement, and their boundaries are also convenient non-seam landmarks. Recorded only at whole-garment scale their boundaries are unresolvable; unrecorded, post-wash shade change is unattributable.

quality.extra: GATE_A. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed print_fade_count integer. DENIM_0001 records 'pronounced whiskering and knee fades' on front thighs/knees, so at least two instances exist there. Lighting must be the rig's standard two diffuse sources: a fade is a low-contrast, large-area shade gradient and any raking light fabricates one.

shots.scale_placement: Board coplanar with the backdrop, top-left frame corner, >=125x100 mm strip in frame, on the backdrop and never on the fade.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on repair instance NN: the whole repair, every repair stitch row, the boundary between repair thread and original fabric, >=40 mm of intact denim on each side, and the nearest seam landmark.
shots.purpose: Repair thread is usually a different fibre from the garment and shrinks at its own rate, so a repair is a local stiffness anomaly that biases any nearby shrinkage or fray measurement. Recording it lets that region be excluded rather than silently averaged in.

shots.scale_placement: Steel rule on the denim beside the repair, coplanar, graduated edge facing it, within 20 mm.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on stain instance NN: the whole stain including its diffuse boundary, >=40 mm of clean denim beyond the outermost visible edge, and the nearest seam landmark. Rig's standard two diffuse sources only -- no raking light, which invents stain edges.
shots.purpose: A stain is the one anomaly expected to shrink or vanish in the wash, so it is a positive control on whether the wash did anything at all, and its before-state extent is the measurand. An unrecorded stain that partially lifts reads afterwards as a new shade gradient.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed stain_count integer.

shots.scale_placement: Steel rule on clean denim beside the stain, coplanar, graduated edge facing it, within 20 mm, never overlapping the stain.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on tear instance NN: the full extent of the tear including both terminations, >=40 mm of intact denim beyond each, any exposed weft floats, and the nearest seam landmark. Do not open, close or flatten the tear -- shoot it as it lies.
shots.purpose: A tear grows in a wash and its terminations migrate, so its before-state length and end-points are the only way to say afterwards whether it grew. Unrecorded, a grown tear is indistinguishable from wash-induced damage the protocol would have to explain.

quality.extra: GATE_B. Instance scheme as in ANOM.DISTRESS; requires the proposed tear_count integer.

shots.framing: 200 mm field centred on unusual-seam instance NN (extra panel seam, non-standard felling, decorative seam, factory join): >=80 mm of the seam run, every topstitch row, both ends or a clear continuation off two frame edges, and >=40 mm of denim each side.
shots.purpose: A seam the standard region list does not name is a ply discontinuity the cut planner does not know about, and the frozen cut line may cross it. If the shears meet an unrecorded seam the cut is neither clean nor reproducible, and the fray measurement at that position is on a different structure from everywhere else on the loop.

shots.scale_placement: Steel rule on the denim beside the seam, coplanar, graduated edge facing it, within 20 mm, not bridging the seam ridge.

shots.framing: Garment turned back-up, left leg laid straight and smoothed, same mount height and board corner as the front frame. Frame the complete back-panel hem edge from the outseam to the inseam seam, plus 120 mm of leg above the hem, board flat in frame, loop tape on the surface 10 mm outboard of the edge with its coordinate continuing from where the front pass ended.
shots.purpose: Completes the original hem loop. PROTOCOL section 5 numbers positions front panel first, then back panel, so the back-panel run is half the loop coordinate and cannot be inferred from the front frame.

quality.extra: OVERHEAD-QA as for the front frame. The hem is a closed LOOP but a flat-laid leg presents it as two stacked runs, so half the loop is only reachable by turning the garment over; the turn is a physical operation, not a digital one, and must be logged as such. It does not trip hem_roughness's resampling rule (that rule is about digital rotation of the mask, EXP_0024), but it does mean the front and back runs were laid twice and may differ in smoothing - log the turn as an explicit step in the ledger.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the hem edge, measured end to end from outseam to inseam seam, must span at least this many px

shots.framing: Turn the left leg inside out (or fold the hem back on itself and hold it flat with a weight placed away from the edge, never a pin) and fill the frame with about 100 mm of the hem allowance seen from the inside: the raw or overlocked cut edge of the allowance, the fold line or lines, every row of stitching, and the thread. Loop tape flat in frame 10 mm from the allowance edge. Optical axis perpendicular to the fabric plane.
shots.purpose: Hem construction determines whether the original hem is a valid finished-edge negative control at all. A single-fold overlocked hem, a double-fold lockstitch hem and a bound hem behave differently in the wash, and a chainstitched hem ropes. Without this frame the negative control is an untyped object and the post-wash comparison against the cut edge has no stated contrast.

quality.extra: MACRO-QA as above. At 0.10 mm/px a typical 3-4 mm stitch pitch is 30-40 px, so stitch type and stitch count are resolvable at the fray-depth ceiling and no finer requirement is needed. The findings this shot supports (fold count, chainstitch vs lockstitch, overlock present, allowance depth in mm) are semantic and no code in this repo can extract them: clipgate's four prompts do not separate them and would in any case be an UNAVAILABLE_CHECK without open_clip weights and network access. They are therefore HUMAN_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED rows recorded with a written 'saw' sentence, and the navigator must not present an unfilled construction row as a pass.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the ~100 mm run of hem allowance imaged along the frame's long dimension must span at least this many px

requires_human: the rule's millimetre graduations are individually separated in this frame (this shot was specified at 0.100 mm/px or finer)

shots.framing: PARAMETERISED OVER LEG. Two frames per leg at the same station and framing: one with the cuff as found (folded), one with the cuff fully unrolled and smoothed flat, both about 100 mm of edge centred on the cuff's mid-front, loop tape in frame. Record the unrolled cuff depth in mm from the tape.
shots.purpose: A cuff hides the true original hem edge and changes the leg-opening circumference the loop arithmetic depends on. Both states must be recorded so the measured circumference is unambiguous and so the finished-edge control is the actual hem rather than a fold.

quality.extra: MACRO-QA as above. The two reps here are the two states (cuffed, uncuffed), not repeatability reps; the generator must label them explicitly in the ledger rather than treating them as interchangeable. CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS.md is explicit that a cuffed or hemmed edge cannot fray however it is washed, so a cuff changes what the original hem is a control FOR.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the ~100 mm run of edge imaged along the frame's long dimension must span at least this many px

requires_human: the rule's millimetre graduations are individually separated in this frame (this shot was specified at 0.100 mm/px or finer)

shots.framing: Garment front-up and conditioned flat. Camera at the grazing station: optical axis in the surface plane, horizontal, perpendicular to the left leg's front-panel hem edge, looking at the hem from beyond the leg opening. A vertical steel rule stands on the surface at the frame centre, zero touching the surface, just outside the fabric. Frame about 100 mm of hem edge in silhouette against a plain dark card standing behind the leg. The stacked front-panel and back-panel edges must both be distinguishable in silhouette; the surface line must be visible across the frame.
shots.purpose: Two measurements at once, neither of which survives the cut: the original hem's total thickness in fabric layers (an independent check on the schema's fabric_thickness_mm, which PROTOCOL section 0.4 otherwise takes from a caliper on a single layer), and the finished hem's baseline edge curl. A finished hem's curl is the zero point against which the post-wash cut edge's curl is read; without it, a post-wash curl number has nothing to be a change from.

quality.extra: GRAZING-QA: the measurand is a displacement normal to the surface, which an overhead camera projects only as a magnification change of order h/D - a 3 mm lift at D = 600 mm is 0.5%, well below the +/-1-2 px endpoint localisation the repo publishes - and the lifted edge occludes the intact-weave reference beneath it, and an overhead mm_per_px derived from a board lying in the surface plane is the wrong scale for anything out of that plane. So profile is the only geometry that measures it. Axis elevation <= 5 deg (UNRELIABLE_TILT_DEG = 5.0, cited from canon/upright.py, not modified). With the axis perpendicular to a straight flat-laid edge run, the edge line is parallel to the image plane, so every point in the frame shares one depth and one scale - that is why a single grazing frame can serve a 100 mm run rather than one position. Never resample, rotate or upright a profile frame. check_image is not applicable at all here: there is no contrasting-backdrop garment blob, so its foreground, exposure and border tests all measure the card or the rule.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the 0-50 mm span of the vertical steel rule must span at least this many px in the image's vertical direction

requires_human: the rule's millimetre graduations are individually separated in this frame (this shot was specified at 0.100 mm/px or finer)

shots.framing: Garment front-up, left leg laid straight and smoothed. Frame the complete front-panel hem edge from the inseam seam to the outseam, plus 120 mm of leg above the hem, plus the ChArUco board lying flat in the same corner of the frame as always. The hem edge must run end to end across the frame with at least 20 mm of backdrop beyond both seam ends. The certified loop tape lies on the surface parallel to and about 10 mm outboard of the hem edge, zero at the inseam seam, graduations legible.
shots.purpose: The original factory hem is the project's own finished-edge negative control: a hemmed edge does not fray however it is washed (CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS.md), and hem_roughness's published negative control is exactly a finished hem (EXP_0024). This frame records that control's geometry at a scale where fray would be visible if it existed, and it is the board-bearing metric anchor for the left leg's hem region. It is also the last chance to record this edge: after the cut the original hem leaves the garment on the offcut and can never be rephotographed in situ.

quality.extra: OVERHEAD-QA: check_image(board, spec) is valid for this shot class (contrasting backdrop, garment is the dominant foreground blob) at quality.py defaults blur_min=80.0, clip_max=0.02, border_max=0.03, mean_range=(40,220), min_corners=12. board.mm_per_pixel is valid because this is near-overhead; never reuse an oblique's value here, and never let capture_watch.py's first-passing-shot backfill (it writes capture_mm_per_px only when it is currently None) supply this number from some other frame. Wrap check_image against the quality.py:40 TypeError (>=12 corners detected, no two adjacent, mm_per_px None) and classify it RETAKE_REQUIRED 'board fragment, no adjacent corners'. board_corners == 0 cannot distinguish 're-aim' from 'board absent'; call cv2.aruco directly if the operator needs that distinction. max_mm_per_px derivation: a 250 mm hem edge spanning the EXP_0016 preferred figure of 800 px is 0.3125 mm/px, floored to 0.30; below ~600 px of that span a frayed and a finished edge measure identically (CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS.md / EXP_0016), so 800 px is the requirement and 600 px the hard floor. This frame also re-certifies the loop tape in situ, because both the board and the tape are in it.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the hem edge, measured end to end from inseam seam to outseam, must span at least this many px

shots.framing: Fill the frame with about 100 mm of hem edge CENTRED on the point where the inseam seam meets the hem. Both the inseam seam running up the leg and the hem edge running across must be visible, with at least 30 mm of each beyond the junction. Certified loop tape flat on the surface 10 mm outboard of the hem edge with its ZERO mark at the junction, graduations legible. Optical axis perpendicular to the fabric plane.
shots.purpose: The inseam seam is the origin of the PROTOCOL section 5 loop coordinate ('starting at the inseam seam'). If its junction with the hem is not imaged at measurement resolution with the tape zero on it, position P01 is an assertion rather than a datum and every later position index inherits that uncertainty. Two repetitions with the camera remounted bound the origin's own repeatability.

quality.extra: MACRO-QA: do not run check_image() unmodified - its foreground is an Otsu split on Lab distance to the border median, so on a frame-filling macro it locks onto the ruler (measured fg=0.100, mean=227, border_fraction=0.329) and returns two confident failures about the wrong object. Take blur_score only, whole-frame, long side resampled to 1500 px exactly as quality.py L58 does, against blur_min=80.0; suppress mean_intensity, border_fraction and foreground_fraction for this shot class. mm_per_px is a person's reading of the certified loop tape, logged with a free-text 'saw' sentence in the data/external/mask_verdicts.json style; no reading means HUMAN_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, never PASS. scale_from_coin is out of range at this scale (its ceiling rmax = 0.05*min(H,W) = 151 px on a 3024 px short side, while a 24.26 mm quarter would be 243 px at the ceiling and ~978 px at a realistic 0.0248 mm/px) and scale_from_grid detects background periodicity, not rulers. A HEIC container is UNAVAILABLE_CHECK ('shoot Most Compatible / export JPEG'), never RETAKE_REQUIRED. Decode with cv2.imread only, which applies EXIF orientation; PIL's .size does not, and mixing them makes every px check disagree on portrait frames. min_board_corners is 0 by geometric necessity, not by relaxation: PROTOCOL section 1's 'board_corners >= 12 for every shot' cannot be met inside a 100 mm frame, because 12 interior corners of this 25.0 mm board need 100 x 125 mm of printed board.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).
quality.subject_px_meaning: the ~100 mm run of hem edge imaged along the frame's long dimension must span at least this many px

requires_human: the rule's millimetre graduations are individually separated in this frame (this shot was specified at 0.100 mm/px or finer)

shots.framing: Fill the frame with about 100 mm of hem edge CENTRED on the point where the outseam (seam or fold) meets the hem. Both the outseam running up the leg and the hem edge running across must be visible with at least 30 mm of each beyond the junction. Loop tape flat on the surface 10 mm outboard of the edge, graduations legible, showing the loop coordinate at which the front pass ends and the back pass begins.
shots.purpose: The outseam is the crossing point between the front-panel and back-panel runs of the loop. PROTOCOL section 5 numbers positions continuously across that crossing, so if it is not imaged the front and back position indices cannot be proven to be one continuous sequence and the loop map has an unverifiable seam.

quality.extra: MACRO-QA as above (blur only, whole-frame at 1500 px long side vs blur_min=80.0; human tape reading for mm_per_px with a 'saw' sentence or HUMAN_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED; HEIC is UNAVAILABLE_CHECK; cv2.imread only; min_board_corners = 0 by board geometry). If the outseam is a selvedge rather than a stitched seam the shot is unchanged but the ledger must record which, because a selvedge outseam does not fray at the junction the way a stitched one does.

shots.framing: PARAMETERISED OVER LEG. Leg inside out or hem folded back, frame about 100 mm of hem allowance centred on the evidence of alteration: a second stitch line, a shortened allowance, a different thread colour or gauge, a residual original crease line, a cut-and-rehemmed raw edge. Loop tape in frame with the alteration's loop coordinate legible.
shots.purpose: A previously shortened leg has a different fabric history at the hem: the surviving allowance may be shallower, the thread different, and the original crease still present. That history is a confound for the finished-hem control and for the garment's original_inseam_cm, and it is unrecoverable once the hem is cut off.

quality.extra: MACRO-QA as above. Identifying an alteration is a human judgement recorded with a written 'saw' sentence in the mask_verdicts.json style; a bare boolean is not enough, because the downstream question is what KIND of alteration and where on the loop.
quality.notes: Author asked for tilt <= 5 deg; carried as a scale_range_ratio limit because degrees need an assumed focal length (EXP_0043).

quality.extra: THE BOARD ON AN OBLIQUE IS A POSE, NOT A SCALE. board.py's mm_per_pixel is the median of adjacent-corner spacings and its own docstring says it is valid for near-overhead shots only — on a 30 degree oblique it returns a confidently wrong number rather than None. Its value must NEVER reach record.json's capture_mm_per_px: capture_watch.py backfills that field from the first passing shot and never overwrites it, so a single oblique processed first would permanently poison the garment's only metric scale with a cosine error that nothing downstream would flag. Stop capture_watch.py's launchd timer for the session or have the navigator own the field. Use solvePnP instead: it gives both the true in-plane scale and the actual viewing angle, which is the only way the '~30 degrees' can be verified at all. POSE ACCEPTANCE: the detected corners must span at least half the board's interior extent on both axes (>= 125 mm of 250 and >= 87.5 mm of 175, both verified) — a pose fitted to less than half the board extrapolates the plane over more than it interpolates. This is a stated design choice, not a measurement. max_tilt_deg 8.0 is the tolerance on DEVIATION FROM THIS SHOT'S NOMINAL 30 degrees, not an absolute tilt: obliques feed no landmark measurement, so EXP_0021's 5 degree landmark result does not bind here; 8.0 is its median subject's >5% threshold and is used only to keep the before, immediate_after and post_wash obliques comparable. Do NOT run check_image: border_max=0.03 is a whole-garment cropping proxy and this frame deliberately shows one leg section, so it would fail by construction.

shots.purpose: A paint film is the feature most likely to be changed by the wash and the feature whose change is most likely to be mistaken for something else — cracking, flaking and edge lift all alter the garment's appearance without any fabric having moved. Without a recorded before state, that pucker is an unexplained difference between the before and post-wash frames.

That makes rivet-to-rivet spacing an internal scale check on any frame containing two of them — independent of the board, and therefore able to catch the case where the board has moved out of the garment's plane. They also matter for a completely different reason: scale_from_coin.py refuses an unmasked frame precisely because rivets read as coins under Hough.

quality.extra: GRAZING-QA. WHY OVERHEAD FAILS, three reasons: (1) the measurand is a displacement normal to the surface and an overhead camera renders it only as a magnification change of order h/D - a 3 mm lift at D = 600 mm is 0.5%, and locally at the edge far less than that, comfortably below the +/-1-2 px endpoint localisation the repo publishes; (2) a curled edge occludes the intact weave beneath it, so the surface datum the measurand is defined against is not even visible from above; (3) an overhead mm_per_px derived from a board lying in the surface plane is the wrong scale for anything lifted out of that plane, so an overhead curl number would be scaled by a factor it has no way to know. SPACING: one profile frame per macro centre, i.e. every 4th position (80 mm of arc), is admissible only while the local edge tangent stays within 18 deg of the image plane across the covered run, because a height on a surface tilted phi reads h*cos(phi) and cos(18.2 deg) = 0.95, the 5% figure EXP_0021 treats as the harm threshold. The covered arc half-width is 0.0505*C - 17.2 mm at C = 340 mm, 20.2 mm at 400 mm, 25.3 mm at 500 mm - so on a curving run at C < 400 mm one frame supports only its centre position and the generator must fall back to one profile frame per 2 cm position; on the straight flat-laid runs the tangent is effectively constant and the full 100 mm frame is valid. Axis elevation <= 5 deg (UNRELIABLE_TILT_DEG = 5.0, cited from canon/upright.py, not modified). check_image is not applicable: there is no contrasting-backdrop garment blob and its foreground, exposure and border tests would all measure the card or the rule. shots.purpose: The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_UPPER.R1. GATE_TEX derivation: a denim warp yarn is roughly 0.4-0.6 mm wide. Two pixels per yarn is only the Nyquist limit -- it detects the twill periodicity but cannot separate a yarn from its neighbour. Eight pixels across the NARROWEST yarn (0.4 mm) is what lets the twill diagonal be traced and a yarn width be measured, giving 0.4/8 = 0.05 mm/px as the ceiling. On a 4032 px long edge that is a 200 mm field; specifying 150 mm leaves margin and lands near 0.037 mm/px, about 11 px per 0.4 mm yarn. The 100 mm clean patch is exactly four ChArUco squares (25.0 mm, protocol/charuco_board.json), so it is directly comparable to a board-scaled measurement. Without this the post-wash weave comparison has no before-state at a scale where shrinkage-driven yarn crowding is visible at all.

shots.purpose: quality.py estimates background colour from an 8 px frame-border ring and splits foreground by Lab distance to that median. Every garment verdict in the whole pilot rests on that assumption. shots.purpose: Every millimetre this project reports comes from square_mm = 25.0 in protocol/charuco_board.json, which is a statement about a PDF, not about the sheet of paper on the table. Consumer printers scale by fractions of a percent and 'fit to page' silently rescales. If the print is 1% small, every mm_per_px, every measurement and the cut position itself are 1% wrong, consistently, and nothing downstream can detect it because the error is common to all frames. Two independent readings follow PROTOCOL §0.4's own 'two readings each' convention.

quality.extra: NOMINAL 250.0 mm, verified not assumed: board.getChessboardCorners() max coordinate is 0.250 m for this spec, i.e. 10 squares x 25.0 mm between the extreme interior corners of the 11-row axis. TOLERANCE +/-1.0 mm. Derivation: a 1 mm-graduated rule is read to +/-0.5 mm at each end, so +/-1.0 mm on a span is the tightest tolerance such a rule can support — the tolerance is set by the instrument, not by preference. +/-1.0 mm on 250.0 mm is 0.4% scale error, which propagates to 4.4 mm over the garment's 1092 mm length (DENIM_0001 front_rise_cm 33.0 + original_inseam_cm 76.2) and therefore sits just ABOVE PROTOCOL §3.2's +/-3 mm mark tolerance: record the measured value and carry the ratio measured/250.0 as a correction on square_mm, do not assume 25.0. Outcomes: |measured-250.0| <= 1.0 -> PASS with the ratio recorded; > 1.0 -> RETAKE_REQUIRED on the print (reprint at 100% scale, tools/make_charuco_board.py says so itself); rule graduations not legible -> RETAKE_REQUIRED; no rule available -> UNAVAILABLE_CHECK. max_mm_per_px 0.5 is Nyquist on the 1 mm graduation. No ruler detector exists, so the reading is HUMAN_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED with the transcribed number and a written 'saw'. Blur over the whole frame, not via check_image (its Otsu foreground locks onto the rule: measured fg=0.100, mean=227, border_fraction=0.329 -> two bogus failures).
